why: Every numeric-named flag is either typed int/float in the binding, or listed here with the reason it is genuinely text. Keys are flag names, or '<tool id>|<flag>' when the reason is specific to one tool. The list is the reviewable record of that judgement: a builder that 'fixes' --worker into an int has to edit this file, so the decision shows up in the diff.

allow_str.--worker: worker/session name, not a count (worktree-harness, agentic-engineering)
allow_str.--workers: list of worker names, argparse nargs='+'
allow_str.--lines: line-range spec such as '10-45', not a count
allow_str.--cores: CPU pin spec such as '4-5' or '4,6,8' (subagent-spaces)
allow_str.--batch: path to a batch JSON file (decide)
allow_str.companion/scripts/companion:doctor|--por: inherited root flag that doctor does not accept; contract-extraction leak, tracked in tier-c

deferred.tailscale-ops: scripts/ts_ops.sh is a bash script with no argparse; --json needs a JSON emitter or a rewrite, not a flag
deferred.guard-hooks: the routable command is a compiled Rust binary (guard-rs/bin/guard-hooks); the Python scripts/guard.py is not what runs, so --json needs a Rust change and a rebuild
